title: Checklist copy + content guidelines for Guided Onboarding / First Production Launch
creator: Tessa Morgan
project: Guided onboarding + first production launch checklist
description: Create the canonical copy rules + final step names/descriptions for the new in-Console onboarding checklist and the matching docs checklist page. Focus: concise step names, consistent tone across Console + docs, and proactive warnings for common onboarding failures (401/403 auth setup, 429 rate limits/quotas, streaming disconnects, usage dashboard lag). Deliverable should be usable by Console engineers implementing UI, Docs team updating IA, and Support creating macros.
content:
Context
- This ticket covers the writing system for the checklist (step name + 1–2 line description + optional “Why it matters” + optional warning), and the rules that keep it consistent across surfaces.
- Inputs: PRD (PM-742), wireframes (DES-418), top onboarding failures (Support Q1 analysis), and dogfood notes.
- Primary surface: Redwood Console checklist component (with step detail drawer). Secondary: docs checklist page and quickstarts.

Goals
1) Make each step immediately understandable to a new engineer skimming the checklist.
2) Reduce avoidable tickets by proactively calling out the “gotchas” at the right moment (auth, quotas/429s, streaming reliability, usage lag).
3) Keep Console microcopy and docs copy aligned: same step names, same ordering, same terminology.
4) Keep copy short enough for the checklist row without truncation in typical viewport sizes.

Non-goals
- Writing full docs content (owned by Docs; we provide the step copy + guidance + snippets for callouts).
- Full in-product guided tours/tooltips (out of MVP).

Audience
- Primary: Software engineers / ML engineers integrating Hosted API.
- Secondary: Team leads doing a “go-live readiness” check (budget/quota, model pinning, fallback, observability).

Voice & tone
- Developer-first, precise, non-marketing.
- Prefer verbs and concrete outcomes over nouns.
- Avoid shaming language (“You forgot…”). Use neutral guidance (“To avoid 401s, set…”).
- Use “you” sparingly; prefer instructional (“Set your API key…”, “Configure retries…”).
- Be explicit when something is optional vs recommended for production.

Terminology standards (must match docs + Console)
- Use “API key” (not “token”).
- Use “project” and “environment” only if those are the actual Console concepts; otherwise use “account” / “API key.”
- Use “quota” for limits; use “budget alerts” for spend guardrails.
- Use “streaming” (not “SSE” unless in advanced detail).
- Use “model version pinning” (not “lock model”).
- Use “fallback policy” (not “failover”) unless we are specifically describing regions.

Length constraints (Console)
- Step name: target 24–32 characters (hard limit: 40 characters; avoid truncation).
- Step description (list view): target 80–110 characters; 1 sentence.
- Step detail drawer: up to ~300 characters before “Read docs” link; avoid long multi-paragraph prose.
- Use callouts sparingly: at most 1 warning callout per step in the detail drawer.

Microcopy patterns
- Status language:
  - Not started: no extra label (status icon only).
  - In progress: “In progress” only when we can reliably infer (avoid if eventing is ambiguous).
  - Completed: “Completed” only when acceptance criteria is met (per event schema).
- Buttons/links:
  - Primary action: verb-first (“Create API key”, “View usage”, “Set budget alert”).
  - Docs link label: “Read how-to” (preferred) or “Read docs” (fallback).
- Warnings:
  - Use “Heads up:” prefix.
  - Keep to one sentence + specific mitigation (“set retries with exponential backoff”).
  - Avoid fear-based phrasing.

Checklist steps (final copy v1)
Note: Step ordering assumes a Hosted API self-serve flow, with later “Production launch” steps framed as recommended before routing real users.

1) Create an API key
- List description: “Generate a key for your project and store it securely.”
- Detail (Why it matters): “Requests without a valid key fail with 401/403.”
- Warning: “Heads up: copying extra whitespace is a common cause of ‘invalid API key’ errors.”
- Deep links: Console → API Keys

2) Set up your environment
- List description: “Add REDWOOD_API_KEY and confirm your base URL/region.”
- Detail: “Use env vars in local dev and secret managers in production.”
- Warning: “Heads up: don’t commit keys to source control.”
- Deep links: Console → API Keys; Docs → Environment variables

3) Make your first request
- List description: “Send a non-streaming request and confirm you receive a 2xx response.”
- Detail: “Start with a small prompt to validate auth, routing, and basic latency.”
- Warning: “Heads up: if you see 401/403, re-check key + org/project selection.”
- Deep links: Docs → Quickstart (language-specific)

4) Try streaming responses
- List description: “Enable streaming and handle partial chunks in your client.”
- Detail: “Streaming improves perceived latency and UX for longer outputs.”
- Warning: “Heads up: plan for disconnects—implement reconnect and resume where supported.”
- Deep links: Docs → Streaming; Examples → Streaming chat reference

5) Set timeouts and retries (recommended)
- List description: “Use sensible timeouts and exponential backoff for transient failures.”
- Detail: “Production clients should treat network failures and 429s as expected.”
- Warning: “Heads up: retrying without backoff can amplify 429 rate limits.”
- Deep links: Docs → Production readiness (SDK); SDK docs → Retry presets

6) Review quotas and rate limits
- List description: “Check your quota and expected throughput to avoid 429s after launch.”
- Detail: “Align limits with peak traffic and add a fallback plan.”
- Warning: “Heads up: 429s often show up only after real traffic ramps—validate before go-live.”
- Deep links: Console → Quotas & Limits; Docs → 429 handling

7) Set budget alerts (recommended)
- List description: “Add budget alerts so spend doesn’t surprise you during testing or launch.”
- Detail: “Use alerts to catch runaway prompts and misrouted traffic early.”
- Warning: “Heads up: usage dashboards can lag; alerts help catch spikes sooner.”
- Deep links: Console → Billing/Usage; Terraform snippet (optional)

8) Pin a model version
- List description: “Pin a model/version so behavior stays stable across provider updates.”
- Detail: “Version pinning reduces regressions from silent model changes.”
- Warning: “Heads up: if you don’t pin, output quality may shift over time.”
- Deep links: Console → Model settings; Docs → Model pinning

9) Configure fallback policy (recommended)
- List description: “Choose what happens when capacity is constrained or errors spike.”
- Detail: “Fallback keeps your app online with a compatible model/region.”
- Warning: “Heads up: define acceptable quality/cost tradeoffs before enabling fallback.”
- Deep links: Console → Routing/Fallback; Docs → Fallback policies

10) Add observability hooks
- List description: “Add request IDs and basic logging so you can debug issues in production.”
- Detail: “Log model, latency, tokens, and error codes (avoid logging prompts with sensitive data).”
- Warning: “Heads up: don’t log API keys or end-user PII.”
- Deep links: Console → Logs/Tracing; Docs → Observability

11) Verify usage in the dashboard
- List description: “Confirm requests/tokens show up in Usage and match your expectations.”
- Detail: “Use this to validate metering and cost before rolling out widely.”
- Warning: “Heads up: dashboards may update with a delay—wait a few minutes before re-testing.”
- Deep links: Console → Usage

Step naming notes / rationale
- “Set timeouts and retries” is intentionally explicit (not “Harden client”): it maps directly to SDK defaults work and top support issues.
- “Review quotas and rate limits” uses both terms: customers search for “rate limit” but the control surface is “quota.”
- “Verify usage in the dashboard” addresses the ‘usage lag’ confusion directly without implying the system is broken.

Console vs Docs alignment rules
- Step names must match exactly (case + phrasing). Docs page headings should use the step name verbatim.
- If docs adds nuance, keep the checklist drawer text stable; add details below the fold in docs.
- Any warning callout in Console should have a corresponding callout section in docs (same heading) for consistency.

Accessibility & clarity checks
- Avoid idioms (“kick the tires”).
- Avoid color-dependent meaning in copy (“in the green”).
- Ensure callouts are meaningful without icons.

Instrumentation considerations (copy implications)
- Copy should not promise completion states we can’t reliably detect.
- Use “recommended” language when completion may be manual/subjective (e.g., “Add observability hooks”).
- Avoid “done” language for budget alerts if the platform can’t confirm alert destinations; prefer “Set budget alerts” and treat completion as ‘configured in Console’.

Deliverables
- Final step names + list descriptions + drawer guidance (above).
- Standard warnings for the top 4 onboarding failures: auth key mistakes, 429s, streaming disconnects, usage dashboard lag.
- Microcopy patterns for links/buttons.

Open questions (resolved)
1) Should we use “Production launch” wording in every step?
- Decision: No. Keep steps action-oriented; reserve “production” for steps that materially reduce go-live risk.

2) Do we mention “idempotency keys” in the retries step?
- Decision: Not in MVP checklist row/drawer. Keep in SDK production readiness docs only.

3) Do we include “Create a project” as a step?
- Decision: No (not universal in current Console). If/when projects/environments become required, revisit in v2.

Review notes / approvals
- 2025-02-20 (Tessa Morgan): Ensure each step reads as an action and has an explicit outcome.
- 2025-02-24 (Dev Patel, Support): Add explicit warning about dashboard lag + 429 surprises; supported.
- 2025-02-26 (Wei Chen, Docs): Agreed on exact step names as H2s; docs IA will redirect older quickstart anchors.
- 2025-03-03 (Dylan Brooks, Eng): Copy length fits wireframe; requested consistent deep link verbs.
- 2025-03-06 (Nikhil Sharma, PM): Requested “fallback policy” phrasing (avoid ‘failover’) to match product terminology.

Follow-ups
- If Dedicated/Private onboarding expands, add variants: ‘Set up networking / allowlists’, ‘Configure SSO/SAML’, ‘Audit logs’, ‘Data residency settings’.
- Add localized copy considerations if/when Console localization starts (not in 2025.04 scope).

Links
- PRD: sources/linear/product-management/PM-742-guided-onboarding-checklist-mvp.json
- Wireframes: sources/linear/design/DES-418-onboarding-checklist-console-wireframes.json
- Metric definitions: sources/linear/product-management/PM-751-define-time-to-first-success-and-first-prod-metrics.json
- Support top issues analysis: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/support-top-issues/top-onboarding-failures-q1-2025.json

Implementation notes for eng
- Please keep row description to a single line; move ‘Why it matters’ + warning into the step drawer.
- If truncation occurs in smaller widths, prefer truncating the description, not the step name.
- Ensure deep-link labels match the verb phrase used in the step name (e.g., “Review quotas and rate limits” → button: “View quotas”).
comments: 2025-02-12 (Kenji Nakamura): Drafting initial step names based on PRD + Support ticket themes. Will propose 2 options for the ‘quotas/rate limits’ step.
2025-02-20 (Priya Shah): Please call out that 429 can happen from both per-minute limits and concurrency; customers interpret it as ‘bug’. Suggest warning copy that it’s expected and actionable.
2025-02-24 (Dev Patel): +1 to adding a dashboard lag callout. We see customers re-run tests repeatedly, increasing spend and confusion.
2025-03-03 (Dylan Brooks): Copy fits the new checklist row spec. Request: standardize docs link label to ‘Read how-to’ across all steps for consistency.
2025-03-06 (Nikhil Sharma): Prefer ‘fallback policy’ over ‘failover’; keep it consistent with routing settings language.
2025-03-28 (Tessa Morgan): Marking Done. Please treat this as the canonical v1 copy source for Console + docs; any changes should be routed back through Design for consistency.
